rationale: Evidence from the baseline race: the robot leaves the line on almost every run. Off-track ends dominate (18 of 20 oval trials, all s-bend and slalom trials), and max_error averages about 0.06 m. That equals the off-track limit, max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.12/4) = 0.06 m, so the robot is failing by exceeding the allowed lateral error, not by stalling. Steering oscillation (about 0.14 to 0.17) and about one line-loss event per run point to over-aggressive steering. The effective turn gain is high: with weights of +/-2 and kp = 2.5, a fully-on-tape outer sensor gives turn = 5, a wheel differential of about 1750 PWM. Base speed 1.3 also carries the robot into bends faster than it can steer. Changes: (1) Narrow the sensor array to x = -0.03 to +0.03 at 0.015 spacing. The outer sensors then still see the 25 mm tape on a centred line, so the signal does not saturate early and recovery is smoother. (2) Reduce kp from 2.5 to 2.0 to cut the overshoot that drives oscillation and the max_error. (3) Raise kd from 0.2 to 0.5 to damp the faster signal changes. (4) Reduce base_speed from 1.3 to 1.1 so the robot holds the line through bends. This costs some time: the 3 s limit needs about 1.5 m/s, so completion may suffer. Accepted because staying on track is worth far more than speed right now. Geometry stays at 0.12 m track, 0.03 m wheels and 0.8 kg mass, and body_width cannot raise the 0.06 m off-track limit within the allowed range. Expected result: fewer off-track ends, max_error below about 0.05, and some s-bend and slalom progress above the baseline 0.12 to 0.17. Hypotheses to test: H1, the off-track failures are mainly from overshoot at bends (check max_error against steering_oscillation). H2, the speed-versus-steering trade-off is the binding limit (check completion_time on runs that finish). Next measurements: max_error, progress, line_loss_events and steering_oscillation per track, to decide between further lowering base_speed and raising kp.
